transcript.text: Good afternoon! This is Mumbai Bank calling regarding your overdue credit card payment. I noticed there is a pending amount on your account. I’d like to remind you that non-payment will badly affect your credit score and may lead to legal action. Can you please let me know when you’ll be able to clear the outstanding balance? If you’re facing any difficulty, I’m here to help.
Hello, thanks for calling. I just want to ask, will this hurt my CIBIL score?

Thank you for asking. Yes, overdue payments do hurt your CIBIL score significantly. Timely payment of your credit card dues is very important for maintaining a good credit score. Non-payment can reduce your score, making it difficult to get loans or other financial products in the future. I suggest clearing your dues at the earliest to avoid any negative impact. Would you like to make the payment today, or do you need assistance with any issues?
Can you tell me how many points exactly will it drop if I don't pay on time?

While the exact drop in your CIBIL score varies from case to case, typically a missed or overdue payment can reduce your score by 50 to 100 points or even more, depending on your overall credit history and the duration of delay. Multiple missed payments have a much greater negative impact—sometimes reducing the score further. 

It's always best to avoid any overdue payments to protect your credit health. Would you like my assistance in clearing the payment today or do you need any help with the amount due?
A friend told me that it drops 100 points every time you miss a payment. Is that really true?

Your friend is partly correct—missing a payment can indeed cause a significant drop, sometimes up to 100 points, especially if your payment history was otherwise good. However, the actual drop depends on your overall credit profile, payment patterns, and how long the payment remains overdue. Sometimes it may be less than 100 points, but repeated missed payments can cause even greater damage over time.

To protect your credit standing, it’s very important to pay as soon as possible. Would you like to proceed with your overdue payment now, or is there any difficulty I can help you with?
Okay, thanks for explaining. I’ll try to clear the payment soon. Can you tell me the total amount I owe right now?

Of course! You currently owe a total of ₹18,750, which includes the principal outstanding, interest at around 12%, and a late fee of ₹1,500. 

If you’d like, I can explore some options to help you settle the amount, including possible discounts on late fees if you’re facing any difficulty. Would you be able to make the full payment today, or would you like to discuss a waiver or installment options?
I understand. I’ll see if I can arrange the full amount soon. One last thing, if I pay late this month, will it affect my score as much as if I never pay at all?

That’s a good question. Paying late does affect your CIBIL score, but it’s always better to pay late than not pay at all. A late payment will cause a drop in your score, but non-payment or letting the dues remain unpaid for a long time can severely worsen your credit score and lead to legal action.

If you clear your dues—even if slightly late—you can gradually improve your score again. May I help you with arranging the payment soon? If needed, I can also provide a waiver on late fees to make it easier for you. Would you like to confirm a payment date now so we can help protect your credit standing?
Okay, thanks for helping out. I’ll try to pay soon to avoid more damage. Could you please send me the payment details via SMS?

Absolutely, I will arrange for the payment details to be sent to your registered mobile number via SMS right away. 

May I confirm that you’ll be able to make the payment within the next 3 days? This will help us update your account accordingly and assist you further if needed. Can I mark your commitment for payment within this period?
Yes, I’ll try my best to make the payment within 3 days. Thanks for your help.
